assays.assay_description: Rats tested individually for 45 min in glass aquaria immediately after i.p. drug administration (8 treatment groups); HTR episodes quantified from video with DeepLabCut/SimBA classifiers. USVs recorded in this phase were too few for statistical analysis and were used only for clustering.

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats were first tested individually for HTR and USVs in glass aquaria

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in the glass aquaria during the 45-min test

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in the glass aquaria during the 45-min test

sample_size.evidence: Sixty-eight drug-naive male Wistar rats; group sizes 8-9 (e.g., AMPH 1 9/9, LSD 0.04 5/8, VEH 7/8)

outcomes.summary: DOI 2.5 mg/kg and LSD 0.08 mg/kg significantly increased HTR episodes versus vehicle; the lower doses of DOI and LSD, lisuride, and amphetamine did not induce HTR.
outcomes.statistics: Kruskal-Wallis KW = 38.24, p < 0.0001; Dunn's post-hoc: DOI 2.5 p < 0.01, LSD 0.08 p < 0.05 vs VEH
outcomes.evidence: Kruskal-Wallis test demonstrated differences between 8 treatments (KW = 38.24, p < 0.0001) and the post-hoc Dunn's multiple comparisons test showed that DOI 2.5 (p < 0.01) and LSD 0.08 (p < 0.05) induced HTR.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Total number of head-twitch response (HTR) episodes recorded during the 45-min test

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Only total HTR counts over the 45-min session reported (median and IQR)

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR (wet-dog shake) is excluded as ethological per rubric; HTR-phase USVs not analysed as outcome

B5_social.evidence: Rats were first tested individually for HTR and USVs in glass aquaria

B6_cognitive.evidence: Acute drug-induced unconditioned response; no learning component

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Video recordings were analyzed using DeepLabCut and SimBA; SimBA-derived classifiers quantified HTR episodes

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter described in glass aquaria

E8_food_water.evidence: not reported; no food/water described in apparatus

D3_recording_days.evidence: HTR tested once in the first phase

D4_baseline.evidence: not reported; drug given immediately before testing

D5_followup.evidence: Testing began immediately after injection; no recording >=24 h post-dose

assays.assay_description: Two weeks after the HTR phase, rats were tested individually for 45 min in black Plexiglas open-field boxes immediately after i.p. drug administration under the same treatment conditions; total distance traveled quantified with DeepLabCut/SimBA.

setup_restrain.evidence: for locomotor activity and USVs in black Plexiglass open-field boxes

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in open-field boxes during the test

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in open-field boxes during the test

sample_size.evidence: One-way ANOVA F(7,60) (68 rats, 8 groups of 8-9)

outcomes.summary: Only amphetamine (1 mg/kg) increased total distance traveled; DOI, LSD and lisuride did not significantly alter locomotor activity (lisuride showed a non-significant tendency to reduce it).
outcomes.statistics: One-way ANOVA F(7,60) = 10.93, p < 0.0001; Holm-Sidak: AMPH 1 p < 0.0001 vs VEH
outcomes.evidence: One-way ANOVA demonstrated significant treatment effects: F(7,60) = 10.93; p < 0.0001 and the Holm-Sidak's multiple comparisons test found increased activity (p < 0.0001) only for the AMPH 1 group.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Total distance traveled during the 45-min locomotor activity test

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Only total distance over 45 min reported

B4_ethological.evidence: Locomotor distance is not an ethological behaviour per rubric

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Video recordings were analyzed using DeepLabCut and SimBA; SimBA-derived classifiers quantified HTR episodes and distance traveled

E7_social_context.evidence: Rats tested individually (Discussion: 'In singly tested rats')

E8_food_water.evidence: not reported; no food/water described in apparatus

D1_continuity.evidence: Total distance traveled during the 45-min locomotor activity test

D3_recording_days.evidence: Open-field tested once in the second phase

D4_baseline.evidence: not reported; drug given immediately before testing

D5_followup.evidence: Drug readministered immediately before OF test; no recording >=24 h after last dose

assays.assay_description: USVs recorded with Avisoft ultrasonic microphones during the 45-min open-field session, detected with DeepSqueak (50-kHz and 22-kHz detectors) and clustered (UMAP-based k-means on 48 VAE/frequency features) into flat, alarm, step-up/trill and upward-ramp clusters. Outcomes: total calls, cluster-specific counts, binary calling, cluster occupancy. HTR-phase USVs were pooled only for clustering.

setup_restrain.evidence: for locomotor activity and USVs in black Plexiglass open-field boxes

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in open-field boxes during recording

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in open-field boxes during recording

sample_size.evidence: Across all 68 rats... AMPH 1 group (9/9), LSD 0.08 group (9/9)... LIS 0.03 group (7/8; 87.5%), LIS 0.3 group (5/8)... LSD 0.04 (5/8), VEH (7/8)

outcomes.summary: Amphetamine and both DOI doses increased total call emission versus vehicle. Occupancy analysis showed DOI (1.25, 2.5 mg/kg) and LSD 0.04 reduced occupancy of the flat-call cluster, whereas LSD 0.08, lisuride 0.03 and amphetamine increased occupancy of frequency-modulated (step-up/trill, upward-ramp) clusters; alarm-call occupancy was unaffected. Cluster-specific count increases reached significance only for amphetamine.
outcomes.statistics: Total calls NB-GLM: LR chi2(7) = 26.86, p < 0.001; AMPH 1 ratio = 59.16 p < 0.01, DOI 1.25 ratio = 16.52 p < 0.05, DOI 2.5 ratio = 30.48 p < 0.01 (Holm). Group x cluster interaction (counts): chi2(21) = 74.08, p < 0.001; AMPH cluster 1 ratio = 64.18 p < 0.05, cluster 3 ratio = 285.15 p < 0.01, cluster 4 ratio = 204.35 p < 0.01. Binary calling Fisher p = 0.05132. Occupancy interaction chi2(21) = 39.62, p < 0.01; cluster 1 lower for DOI 1.25, DOI 2.5, LSD 0.04 (p < 0.01); cluster 3 higher for AMPH 1, LIS 0.03, LSD 0.08 (p < 0.001); cluster 4 higher for LIS 0.03 (p < 0.01), LSD 0.08 (p < 0.001).
outcomes.evidence: Total call emission increased after amphetamine and both DOI doses... DOI and LSD (0.04 mg/kg) reduced occupancy of the flat-call cluster... In contrast, LSD (0.08 mg/kg), lisuride (0.03 mg/kg), and amphetamine increased occupancy of frequency-modulated clusters

B1_num_measures.evidence: Total calls, cluster-specific call counts (4 clusters), binary calling, and cluster occupancy (4 clusters) reported

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Calls summed over the 45-min session; no within-session time course

B4_ethological.evidence: USVs are species-typical vocalizations directly measured (22-kHz alarm and 50-kHz calls)

B5_social.evidence: In singly tested rats... calls cannot be determined to reflect any specific communicative signal

B7_automated_classification.evidence: USVs were detected using DeepSqueak and clustered in a custom, unsupervised manner using variational autoencoder-based, and frequency-based embeddings

B8_multivariate.evidence: UMAP-based k-means, PCA, t-SNE, HDBSCAN, hierarchical clustering and Bray-Curtis PCoA of occupancy profiles

E7_social_context.evidence: In singly tested rats LSD, lisuride, and amphetamine increased occupancy of frequency-modulated clusters

E8_food_water.evidence: not reported; no food/water described in apparatus

D1_continuity.evidence: Treatment-effect USV analyses derive from the open-field session; 'calling during HTR testing was too low to be examined statistically... served only for clustering'

D3_recording_days.evidence: USV outcomes analysed from one open-field session per rat

D4_baseline.evidence: not reported; drug given immediately before testing

judge_notes: Retained three assays (modal across deepseek4 and gemma4): HTR in glass aquaria, locomotor activity in open field, and USV recording; USVs are a distinct behavioural domain (vocal) from locomotion even though recorded in the same apparatus. Rejected qwen's merging of USV outcomes into both HTR and locomotor assays (inflated B1/B4/B8 there).

USV assay scored as single session/1 day (deepseek4) rather than multiple sessions (gemma4): HTR-phase USVs were pooled only for clustering and not analysed for treatment effects, and that phase used a different apparatus.
Corrected gemma4's USV B1 value label to '7+' to match score 3 (total calls, 4 cluster counts, 4 occupancies, binary calling).

B7=1 for HTR and locomotion because DeepLabCut pose estimation + SimBA classifiers were used; B7=1 for USVs because DeepSqueak deep-learning detection plus unsupervised call-type clustering classifies vocal behaviour.
Age set to not_reported: only body weight at delivery (151-175 g) given; qwen's juvenile inference rejected per no-inference rule.
Dosing includes lisuride and amphetamine as administered comparator compounds (modal across deepseek4 and gemma4).

Locomotor direction set to no_effect for psychedelics (only amphetamine increased activity); USV direction 'mixed' since DOI increased total calls but reduced flat-call occupancy while LSD 0.08 increased FM-call occupancy.
Food/water restriction set to 'during' per rubric default for standard short-test apparatus; confidence medium since not explicitly stated.
